reason: The patch applies cleanly with `git am` onto a fresh clone of origin/main @ be917d0 (single commit, 9 files, no conflicts). I re-ran every claim independently using my own tezcatl-CLI-compatible shim (playwright + Chromium 1194, NOT the worker's puppeteer shim) plus an offline import map for verbspec/zod/@std/assert: the scout verify_command passes verbatim (both mocks: `drift ✓ · audit ✓ · cvd ✓ · axe ✓`, exit 0; injected copy: 3 violations html-has-lang/image-alt/link-name, cli.ts `axe` returns ok:false, 'OK: axe gate failed closed'). The exact CI invocations also behave as claimed: macOS-job flags (`--allow-read --allow-write --allow-run` only) still run axe via the widened subprocess; Linux-job `AXE_SKIP=1` yields `axe ⊘` exit 0; missing binary (TEZCATL=/nonexistent, or tezcatl absent from PATH) fails closed with exit 1 through both axe.ts and check.ts. `deno test axe.test.ts resolve.test.ts` = 10 passed; without tezcatl the 2 axe tests are `ignored`, not silently passed. `deno check` is clean on cli/check/axe/axe.test and the touched dependents. The tezcatl CLI contract (`<url> --wait=MS --eval=JS`, prints eval result, exit 1 on error, `--version`) matches georgemandis/tezcatl v0.3.0 source and the flake pins 0.3.0 with mainProgram=tezcatl; action SHAs match site-ci.yml's existing pins. Issue #1's acceptance items (axe verb in cli.ts, tezcatl render, embedded axe-core, zero-violation assertion, wired into check.ts and tokens-check.yml) are all literally present. Two things keep confidence at medium rather than high: (1) nothing has run on real WebKit — the macOS `axe` job is unexecuted and the only proof is Chromium; (2) the issue's stated purpose ('proves the derived AAA is real') is only partially served — the gate asserts A/AA, and I confirmed the worker's reason is factual (with wcag2aaa + color-contrast-enhanced the vendored axe flags a/button/small at 5.25–5.47:1 on both mocks, matching ROLE_CONTRACT's aaText tier for link/muted/on-accent), so a strict-AAA gate would fail main by design; the worker disclosed this rather than hiding it. The vendored axe.min.js sha256 matches the value recorded in axe.ts and its header reads axe v4.12.1, but its provenance could not be independently confirmed here (npm/CDN/raw.githubusercontent all 403 through the proxy) — the maintainer must do that check.

The macOS `axe` CI job has never executed; first real-WebKit proof happens on the PR run. The Linux job's `deno check *.ts` now also typechecks axe.test.ts (jsr:@std/assert@^1 already in deno.lock, so no lock change).
check.ts prints an empty `axe:   ` line when axe.ts dies before its summary (e.g. tezcatl missing) because it reads the last stdout line; the stderr reason still follows, cosmetic only.
axePage retries only on empty output, not on a non-zero tezcatl exit; a transient WebKit failure fails the gate rather than retrying — acceptable for fail-closed, worth knowing.
